scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone” (preprints/An-Exact-Semidefinite-Lift-of-a-Nonspectrahedral-Hyperbolicity-Cone-October-5-2026/Exact-Semidefinite-Lift-of-a-Nonspectrahedral-Hyperbolicity-Cone.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 095 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b16fbcc207da5cc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist fixed matrices A1, . . . , A23, B1, . . . , B307 ∈ S100 such that, for every x = (X, Z, y) ∈ V, x ∈ K ⇐⇒ there exists v ∈ R307 with 23 X ν=1 xνAν + 307 X j=1 vjBj ⪰ 0. The equivalence holds on the entire closed cone, including points with singular X.
